tensions.topic: Was finite-coefficient recovery of the hyperbolic singular set an open problem?

expert_A.position: Open. Verbatim: 'Restricted to hyperbolic 2-orbifolds, the results [DGGW] state don't yield complete information about the singular set. All this information is there... presumably it could be extracted... by looking at higher and higher terms in the asymptotic expansion.' Note 'higher and higher' - unbounded, no threshold.

expert_B.position: Claims to give the first exact finite-coefficient determinacy threshold for a family of hyperbolic cone orbifolds.

tensions.reading: These agree rather than conflict, and A is strong independent support for B. A specialist source states the problem was open in exactly the terms B claims to close.

tensions.topic: Who established qualitative cone-order determinacy for hyperbolic orbisurfaces?

expert_A.position: The Laplace spectrum of a compact hyperbolic 2-orbifold determines the number of cone points of each order (plus volume, mirror length, geodesics). Selberg trace formula, full spectrum.

expert_B.position: Same conclusion for orientable constant-curvature orbisurfaces, generalizing Dryden-Strohmaier from kappa=-1 to all kappa != 0.

tensions.reading: No conflict, but a priority ordering the manuscript misses: for the HYPERBOLIC case Doyle-Rossetti is six years earlier. Sec 1.3(a) attributes the fact to Ucar alone.

expert_A.position: b_{1/2} = (5/(96 sqrt(pi))) sum kappa_i cot(alpha_i), a rational closed form.

expert_B.position: Identifies a computational error - 'the pole of Gamma at s=0 seems to have been ignored' - and proves the correct b_{1/2}(C) is irrational in f'(0).

tensions.reading: B supersedes A. The manuscript cites Suleymanova's OTHER paper (arXiv:1701.01874), so it is not directly affected, but it should not lean on 1711.00577.

tensions.topic: Do curved-cone results bear on constant-curvature orbifold cones?

expert_A.position: They do not - a constant-curvature orbifold cone has no curvature blow-up at the tip.

expert_B.position: Confirms it, and more strongly: f''(0)=0 identically for ANY orbifold cone point, constant curvature or not. Verbatim: 'Passing to an orbifold cone point of order n just corresponds to passing from f to f/n, so f''(0)=0 still holds for cone points in orbisurfaces.' Hence b_{1/2}(C)=0 there.

tensions.reading: Agreement, and the manuscript's claim is if anything understated. Cite the specific statement.

tensions.topic: How strong a stability modulus is achievable in inverse spectral geometry?

expert_A.position: Log-type, on a smooth warped product.

expert_B.position: Triple-logarithmic, for orbifold reconstruction from interior spectral data.

tensions.reading: Both are far weaker than the explicit algebraic constants the manuscript plans. Not a contradiction - the manuscript recovers a FINITE DISCRETE invariant, not a continuous metric, which is why it can do better. Worth saying explicitly so the strength does not read as an overclaim.
